youtube.title: duel — two acoustic guitar players trading solos, six exchanges
youtube.description:
Acoustic guitar duel: two steel-string players trading six solos in E dorian at 125 BPM, over acoustic bass, cajon and shakers. Every note is written by hand, none generated.

Two players, not two sounds. One is tight and bright, close-miked and dry, legato, accenting on the beat, sitting left. The other is looser, warmer, roomier, punchier in the attack, leaning on the offbeats, sitting right. They play together in the intro, verse, break and pickup, then answer each other solo for solo. In three of the six exchanges they step on each other, the next player coming in under the last bar while the first refuses to stop. The finale ends the duel together, one on the coda's line a third up, the other pulsing beneath it.

Written as text, mixed by measurement, rendered in the browser.

Chapters
0:00 Intro and verse
0:23 First exchange
0:38 The answer
0:53 Second exchange
1:09 The answer
1:24 Break
1:32 Third exchange
1:47 The answer
2:03 Fourth exchange
2:18 The answer
2:33 Pickup into the fifth
2:53 The answer, both at once
3:08 Coda, both players
3:23 Outro

Play and edit this song in your browser at jonborchardt.github.io/strudel-bench — press play, drag a slider, change a note, hear it immediately. Nothing to install. 

Every song here is a text file. This one is songs/duel.strudel in the repo, along with the harness that plays it:
https://github.com/jonborchardt/strudel-bench

strudel-bench is a live-coding harness where a song is a text file written in a high-level language: parts, sections, and twelve musical axes (density, brightness, weight, space, articulation and so on) that a phrase like "darker and more spacious" can move. Most of the code and the songs were written by coding agents working from a written spec, in the spirit of my blog, "always shippable, always improving":
https://jonborchardt.github.io/blog/

The video is not a screen recording. It is generated from the song itself: every hit in the music drives the animation, and the world it plays in is chosen from the song's own musical features.

Built on Strudel, the JavaScript port of TidalCycles: https://strudel.cc
Samples come from the public Strudel packs, each under its own license: https://strudel.cc/learn/samples/

prompt: porch with a second, nylon guitar: alongside the steel in the ensemble sections, dueling it solo for solo, together at the end

requests.ask: a new copy of porch, keep porch as is; add a second guitar of a different quality that plays alongside the first in intro, verse, break, pickup, outro, and plays its own solo on solob, solo2b ... solo6b, like dueling guitars

changes.why: second guitar gm_acoustic_guitar_nylon as melody2: darker (brightness .7), a little wetter, position .3 against the picking at -.35, humanize 15 ms
chord tones between the steel's picking, an octave up; the outro's last bar a held root
the hook a third above the steel
the run a third below the steel

the nylon's answers: the opening cell turned over and a question on the fifth; lower and off the beat then climbing; double-stops held across the beat; the climb answered by a fall; the fifth in kind a third under the steel's shapes
the climax, the duel ending together: the nylon on the coda's line, the steel the same line a third above, a two-bar fill
measured solo, solob and solo6b: the nylon sits 2.8 dB under its mix like the steel's 2.7, the finale's two guitars within a dB; nothing to change

requests.ask: make them both acoustic steel, in two places in the room, with enough character to tell two players apart; and have some solos step on each other, the next starting as the other finishes

changes.why: player two on gm_acoustic_guitar_steel:5, the LK steel font: a different sampled guitar under the same GM name
player one: brightness .85, space .35, position -.3, articulation .45 (legato), humanize 8 ms / .08 per phrase, accents on the beat
player two: brightness .6, space .55, position .35, articulation .65 (a punchier attack), humanize 22 ms / .18 per bar, accents off the beat (V2 '.75 1 .8 .95 ...')
-.35>-.12: the picking just left of centre so the two players have the sides

solo4/solo4b, solo5/solo5b the overlaps: player two enters under the last bar (two bars in the fifth) with a run into its first note, player one hangs a bar (two, the high root tremolo then held, in the fifth) over the answer

player two postgain 1.8: the LK font measured 5 dB under the first (8 dB under the mix where player one sits 3); level tops at 2, postgain is superdough's last gain; after it both players sit 3-4 dB under their mixes

requests.ask: in solo6b the notes get too silly: player two's coda part; player one's coda3 is fine

changes.why: CODA>CODA2: player two no longer doubles the coda line under player one's thirds (the hemiola ran in parallel thirds and the double-stop bar stacked four notes); it plays the hemiola's accents as a 3-against-4 pulse on the root, the 3+2+3 bar as single notes, held chord tones under the rising sequence, and the same landing on the root

requests.ask: finish the mixing pass: measure the sections not yet measured

changes.why: measured intro, verse, break, pickup, solo2b, solo3b, solo4b: all mix-lint clean; the two guitars' masking in verse, break and pickup (.3 in every band) is the harmonized hook itself, the same rhythm in thirds, not a collision
level 1.2>.8, break.melody2 1.1>.9, pickup.melody2 1.6>1.2: the harmony sat within a dB of the lead; now 4 dB under in the verse, 2.4 in the pickup
the mix lint's 'melody dominates' stands: two guitars alone and the lead is most of what is heard, which is the point of the pickup
